report.source_text: The initial spiral CT scan of the lungs, mediastinum, abdomen, and pelvis with and without contrast revealed an enlarged heterogeneously enhancing solid mass located at the mid to lower pole of the left kidney, measuring 70 mm × 75 mm × 105 mm with tumor thrombosis extending into the left renal vein and IVC superiorly over a craniocaudal length of ~23 cm, terminating below the right atrium. In addition, mild hypodense fluid was noted in the pelvic cavity. Pulmonary findings revealed filling defects in the right main pulmonary artery and its segmental branches, consistent with pulmonary thromboembolism and a 7 mm ground-glass nodule detected in the left lower lobe (LLL) superior segment.

report.source_text: The patient’s postoperative course was largely uneventful, aside from some minor incisional pain, which was well managed with analgesics. She was discharged 1 week after the operation in stable condition with appropriate follow-up care. She initiated systemic chemotherapy as part of her comprehensive treatment plan 2 months postoperatively. Given the prothrombotic risk associated with both malignancy and chemotherapy, she has remained on anticoagulant therapy since her initial admission.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old female presented with progressive shortness of breath and was initially suspected of pulmonary embolism and anticoagulated. Chest CT revealed pulmonary emboli, a pulmonary nodule, and a large left renal mass with tumor thrombosis extending into the left renal vein and IVC. Nephrectomy was performed. Histopathology showed a small round blue cell tumor with sheet-like infiltration. Immunohistochemistry was positive for NKX2.2, CD99, synaptophysin, and chromogranin, and negative for several other markers. FISH detected an EWSR1 gene rearrangement (t(11;22)) confirming peripheral PNET/Ewing sarcoma. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and she commenced systemic chemotherapy while continuing anticoagulation. The tumor necrosis percentage was not documented in available sources.
